rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this candidate raises SecurityGain/DiversityGain across all seven passes while keeping cost dimensions bounded. SUB and SPLIT get the highest security/diversity weights because they are near-free transformations that should blanket every function, including the 40KB init routine where cheap broad-surface obfuscation pays off most. FLA keeps a strong SecurityGain (0.8) to obscure the search-kernel loop structure but its RuntimeCost weight stays at 0.6 since Searching-dbl is a hot-loop runtime benchmark where flattening dispatch overhead is the main risk; BCF similarly gets solid security weight with a tempered SizeCost (0.55) given the tiny 43KB text section leaves room for growth. IBR/ICALL/IGV carry moderate weights: they add real indirectness that resists static analysis of the searching loops and global array accesses, but their RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights are held below the loop-critical passes so the optimizer can still handle the double-precision kernels safely and the correctness property that held in round 0 is preserved.
